content: Omeprazole interacts with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly through CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 pathways. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Sparsentan: As a CYP2C19 inducer, sparsentan reduces the exposure and efficacy of CYP2C19 substrates, including omeprazole. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. St. John’s Wort: This herbal supplement decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Stiripentol: Being both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, stiripentol can increase omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates may be necessary if adverse effects occur. 4. Tacrolimus: Omeprazole increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, particularly in intermediate or poor metabolizers. Caution and monitoring of whole blood concentrations are required. 5. Tazemetostat: Omeprazole increases tazemetostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while tazemetostat decreases omeprazole levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Tinidazole: Omeprazole increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Tofacitinib: Omeprazole increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. No specific dose adjustment is recommended unless co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors, in which case a dose reduction is necessary. 8. Triclabendazole: Omeprazole levels are increased by triclabendazole through CYP2C19 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Vismodegib: Omeprazole decreases vismodegib levels by increasing gastric pH, which alters solubility and bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor. 10. Voriconazole: This antifungal increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 11. Warfarin: Omeprazole increases warfarin levels by inhibiting the metabolism of its R-enantiomer via CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 12. Acetazolamide: This drug increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 13. Alprazolam: Omeprazole increases alprazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 14. Ambrisentan: Omeprazole increases ambrisentan levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 15. Anastrozole: This drug increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 16. Bismuth Subsalicylate: Omeprazole increases bismuth subsalicylate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 17. Blessed Thistle: This herbal supplement decreases omeprazole effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The interaction is theoretical and of unknown significance. 18. Bosentan: Omeprazole levels are decreased by bosentan through CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unknown. 19. Carbamazepine: Omeprazole increases carbamazepine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. 20. Chlordiazepoxide: Omeprazole increases chlordiazepoxide levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Clomipramine: Omeprazole increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Clonazepam: Omeprazole increases clonazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Clorazepate: Omeprazole increases clorazepate levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Cyanocobalamin (Vitamin B12): Omeprazole decreases cyanocobalamin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Cyclophosphamide: Omeprazole levels are increased by cyclophosphamide through CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Danazol: This drug increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Darifenacin: Omeprazole levels are decreased by darifenacin through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Devil’s Claw: This herbal supplement decreases omeprazole effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The interaction is theoretical and of unknown significance. 29. Dexamethasone: Omeprazole levels are decreased by dexamethasone through CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Diazepam: Omeprazole increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 31. Dronedarone: This drug increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Drospirenone: Omeprazole levels are increased by drospirenone through CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 33. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: No clinically significant interactions with omeprazole have been observed or are expected based on drug interaction studies. 34. Eslcarbazepine Acetate: This drug decreases omeprazole effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for gastrointestinal symptoms. 35. Estazolam: Omeprazole increases estazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Etravirine: Omeprazole increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Ferric Carboxymaltose: Omeprazole decreases ferric carboxymaltose levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 38. Fluoxetine: This antidepressant increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Flurazepam: Omeprazole increases flurazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 40. Glipizide: Omeprazole increases glipizide levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Larotrectinib: This drug increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 42. Levoketoconazole: Omeprazole levels are increased by levoketoconazole through CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Levothyroxine: Omeprazole decreases levothyroxine levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 44. Liothyronine: Omeprazole decreases liothyronine levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 45. Liotrix: Omeprazole decreases liotrix levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 46. Lisdexamfetamine: Omeprazole reduces the time to maximum concentration (Tmax) for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine due to reduced gastric acidity. Monitor for changes in clinical effects. 47. Lorazepam: Omeprazole increases lorazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 48. Methamphetamine: Omeprazole decreases methamphetamine levels through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for changes in clinical effects. 49. Midazolam: Omeprazole increases midazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 50. Mitotane: This drug decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for possible dosage adjustments. 51. Ospemifene: Omeprazole increases ospemifene levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 52. Phytoestrogens: Omeprazole decreases phytoestrogen levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 53. Ponatinib: Omeprazole decreases ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 54. Quazepam: Omeprazole increases quazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Ribociclib: This drug increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 56. Ruxolitinib: Omeprazole increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Theophylline: Prolonged use of omeprazole may increase the toxicity of theophylline by altering gastrointestinal motility. Monitor for toxicity. 58. Thyroid Desiccated: Omeprazole decreases thyroid desiccated levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 59. Triazolam: Omeprazole increases triazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 60. Abrocitinib: Omeprazole increases abrocitinib levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 61. Acalabrutinib: Omeprazole decreases acalabrutinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Apalutamide: This drug decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute another drug. 63. Armodafinil: Omeprazole levels are increased by armodafinil through CYP2C19 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 64. Atazanavir: Omeprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Avapritinib: Omeprazole increases avapritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 66. Axitinib: Omeprazole increases axitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 67. Belumosudil: Omeprazole decreases belumosudil levels by increasing gastric pH. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
